messages.subject: Modeling continuous items
parts:
Hello,

I have an assessment with 40 items. The first 15 are continuous and the last 25 are Likert-type items. This is a five-factor scale with the model specified below. Is there a way to model these continuous items in the mirt package?

m<-
'F1 = 3,9,14,17,31:35
F2 = 5,6,11,26:30
F5 = 1,8,13,21:25
F4 = 4,7,12,16:20
F5 = 2,10,15,36:40'

model<-mirt.model(m)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Modeling continuous items
parts:
Unfortunately not, sorry. Continuous IRT models are not supported in the package because it is difficult to merge continuous and categorical data in IRT. You may have better luck using something like the lavaan package for this sort of structure. Cheers.

Phil
